stages.name: Tribute-paying states
stages.desc: Local kings keep their thrones and send tribute

stages.name: Phoenician workshop cities
stages.desc: Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and their colonies: ivory, purple cloth, trade

stages.name: North Syrian workshop kingdoms
stages.desc: Neo-Hittite and Aramaean courts with their own ivory carvers

stages.name: Annexed provinces
stages.desc: Ruled by Assyrian governors; people deported

stages.name: Assyrian core
stages.desc: The land of Ashur and its royal cities

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: Cypriot kingdoms trading with the Levant
Tyrians settle at Kition and build a temple of Astarte
Seven kings of Cyprus submit; Sargon II's stele is set up at Kition
Esarhaddon lists ten kings of Cyprus among his vassals

states.name: Israel
timeline: The kingdom of Israel under Omri; Philistine cities on the coast
Ahab of Israel fields two thousand chariots against Assyria at Qarqar
Jehu pays tribute to Shalmaneser III
Galilee is annexed as the province of Megiddo
Ashdod's revolt is crushed and the city made a province

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Samaria, Israel's new capital, and the kingdom of Judah in the hills
Jehu's tribute, later carved on the Black Obelisk
Hanunu of Gaza flees to Egypt; Ahaz of Judah becomes a vassal
Samaria falls and becomes the province of Samerina; Judah stays a vassal
Sennacherib ravages Judah; Hezekiah sends ivory couches to Nineveh

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon and Byblos: Phoenician cities trading across the Mediterranean
Phoenician kings send Ashurnasirpal II gold, linen, ebony and ivory
Hiram of Tyre pays tribute; the northern coast is annexed as Simirra
Luli, king of Sidon and Tyre, flees to Cyprus before Sennacherib
Esarhaddon razes Sidon and makes it an Assyrian province
Tyre is blockaded and its king Baal submits

states.name: Syria
timeline: Aramaean and Neo-Hittite kingdoms: Bit Adini, Arpad, Hamath, Damascus
Ashurnasirpal II marches through to the sea; Syrian kings pay tribute
Bit Adini is annexed; Til Barsip becomes Kar-Shalmaneser
Shalmaneser III besieges Hazael in Damascus
Damascus pays Adad-nirari III a tribute that includes ivory beds
Arpad falls after a three-year siege and becomes a province
Damascus is annexed and its king Rezin killed
Sargon II crushes Hamath's revolt at Qarqar

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Neo-Hittite kingdoms of the southeast: Carchemish, Sam'al, Gurgum, Kummuh; Urartu beyond
Carchemish pays tribute to Ashurnasirpal II
Sargon II annexes Carchemish and carries off its treasury
Gurgum and Melid become Assyrian provinces
Kummuh is annexed

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Ashurnasirpal II rules from Ashur and Nineveh; Babylonia in the south stays independent
Kalhu (Nimrud) is inaugurated as the new royal capital
Tiglath-Pileser III takes the crown of Babylon
Nabopolassar seizes Babylon; the south breaks away
The Medes sack Ashur and attack Nimrud
Nineveh and Nimrud are sacked; the Assyrian empire collapses

states.name: Iran
timeline: Mannaeans, Medes and Elam in the Zagros and beyond
Tiglath-Pileser III campaigns in the Zagros; Median chiefs send horses
Ashurbanipal sacks Susa, the capital of Elam
Cyaxares unites the Medes against Assyria

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ammon, Moab and Edom, kingdoms east of the Jordan
Mesha of Moab throws off Israelite rule
Ammon, Moab and Edom pay tribute to Tiglath-Pileser III
Northern Gilead is annexed; the southern kingdoms remain vassals

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Egypt under Libyan pharaohs; a route for African ivory and ebony
An Egyptian army is beaten alongside Gaza at Raphia
Esarhaddon takes Memphis; Delta rulers become vassals
Ashurbanipal sacks Thebes
Psamtik I unites Egypt and ends Assyrian overlordship

states.name: N. Cyprus
timeline: Kingdoms of eastern Cyprus, among them Salamis
The kings of Cyprus send gifts to Sargon II

events.title: Ashurnasirpal II
events.text: Ashurnasirpal II becomes king of Assyria at Ashur and begins yearly campaigns of conquest and terror.

events.title: Banquet at Kalhu
events.text: The king opens his new capital at Kalhu (Nimrud) with a feast he says fed 69,574 guests.

events.title: Phoenician tribute
events.text: On the Mediterranean shore the kings of Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arwad send gold, linen, ebony and ivory.

events.title: Carchemish submits
events.text: Sangara of Carchemish, a Neo-Hittite king, pays tribute as the Assyrian army crosses the Euphrates.

events.title: Til Barsip taken
events.text: Shalmaneser III annexes Bit Adini and renames its capital Kar-Shalmaneser.

events.title: Battle of Qarqar
events.text: A Syrian and Levantine coalition, including Ahab of Israel, halts Shalmaneser III on the Orontes.

events.title: Fort Shalmaneser
events.text: An arsenal and treasury is built at Nimrud; its storerooms will later hold thousands of ivories.

events.title: Jehu's tribute
events.text: Jehu of Israel bows before Shalmaneser III, a scene carved on the Black Obelisk.

events.title: Hazael besieged
events.text: Shalmaneser III besieges Damascus; an ivory naming its king Hazael was later found at Nimrud.

events.title: Mesha of Moab
events.text: King Mesha frees Moab from Israel and records it on a basalt stele at Dibon.

events.title: Tyrians at Kition
events.text: Phoenicians from Tyre settle at Kition on Cyprus and build a temple of Astarte.

events.title: Damascus pays
events.text: Adad-nirari III takes tribute from Damascus, including an ivory bed and an inlaid ivory couch.

events.title: Tiglath-Pileser III
events.text: A usurper takes the Assyrian throne and turns tribute-paying states into provinces.

events.title: Zagros campaign
events.text: Assyrian armies march into the Zagros and take horses from Median chiefs.

events.title: Arpad falls
events.text: After a three-year siege, the Aramaean kingdom of Arpad becomes an Assyrian province.

events.title: Tribute of kings
events.text: Hiram of Tyre, Rezin of Damascus and Menahem of Israel pay tribute; Simirra becomes a province.

events.title: Gaza campaign
events.text: Tiglath-Pileser III marches down the coast; Hanunu of Gaza flees to Egypt.

events.title: Damascus annexed
events.text: Damascus falls, its king Rezin is killed and its people are deported.

events.title: Galilee annexed
events.text: Northern Israel becomes the province of Megiddo; thousands are deported.

events.title: King of Babylon
events.text: Tiglath-Pileser III takes the hands of the god Marduk and the crown of Babylon.

events.title: Samaria falls
events.text: Israel's capital, famed for its 'house of ivory', falls; Sargon II claims 27,290 deportees.

events.title: Hamath crushed
events.text: Sargon II defeats Hamath at Qarqar and flays its king Yau-bi'di.

events.title: Battle of Raphia
events.text: Sargon II defeats Gaza and an Egyptian army on the border of Egypt.

events.title: Carchemish annexed
events.text: Sargon II deposes Pisiri and carries the treasury of Carchemish to Kalhu.

events.title: Musasir looted
events.text: Sargon II plunders the temple of the god Haldi at Musasir, listing every treasure taken.

events.title: Ashdod revolt
events.text: The Philistine city of Ashdod rebels and is made an Assyrian province.

events.title: Stele at Kition
events.text: Sargon II's stele is set up on Cyprus as seven Cypriot kings submit.

events.title: Dur-Sharrukin
events.text: Sargon II inaugurates his new capital at Khorsabad, a year before his death in battle.

events.title: Luli flees
events.text: Luli, king of Sidon and Tyre, flees by sea to Cyprus as Sennacherib advances.

events.title: Lachish falls
events.text: Sennacherib storms Lachish, the second city of Judah, and deports its people.

events.title: Hezekiah's tribute
events.text: Hezekiah of Judah sends gold, silver, ivory couches, ivory chairs and elephant hides to Nineveh.

events.title: Babylon destroyed
events.text: Sennacherib sacks Babylon and floods its ruins.

events.title: Sidon razed
events.text: Esarhaddon destroys Sidon, beheads its king Abdi-Milkuti and builds a new Assyrian town.

events.title: Ten kings of Cyprus
events.text: Esarhaddon lists the kings of Salamis, Paphos and eight other Cypriot cities as vassals.

events.title: Memphis taken
events.text: Esarhaddon storms Memphis and drives the Kushite pharaoh Taharqa south.

events.title: Thebes sacked
events.text: Ashurbanipal's army sacks Thebes and carries its treasures to Nineveh.

events.title: Egypt breaks free
events.text: Psamtik I of Sais unites Egypt and ends Assyrian overlordship.

events.title: Susa sacked
events.text: Ashurbanipal destroys Susa, capital of Elam, and plunders its tombs and temples.

events.title: Nabopolassar
events.text: A Chaldean leader seizes Babylon and begins a long war against Assyria.

events.title: Ashur falls
events.text: The Medes under Cyaxares storm Ashur, Assyria's oldest city, and attack Nimrud.

events.title: Nineveh falls
events.text: Medes and Babylonians take Nineveh after a three-month siege.

events.title: Nimrud burns
events.text: Kalhu is sacked; gold is stripped from the ivories and broken pieces end up in wells.

chartNote: Share of the mapped area, by each present-day country's relation to Assyria. Regions are today's boundaries, not ancient ones: one modern country often held several kingdoms with different fates, and the map shows the one that matters most to the ivories. Large Egypt, Iran and Turkey swing the shares. Ancient dates are approximate, often by a year or two.
